name: vscode-idris2
description: Idris 2 support for Visual Studio Code: highlighting, editing support, snippets and toolchain setup so far; checking with the compiler is planned (see the README).

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In Restricted Mode the extension runs no program: it does not start idris2, idris2-lsp or pack, not even to read their versions, and it reads .ipkg files with a limited built-in reader instead of the compiler. Highlighting, snippets and editing support work as usual. Workspace values of the idris2.toolchain paths and environment apply only once the workspace is trusted.

idris2.toolchain.idris2Path.markdownDescription: Path to the `idris2` executable. Empty (the default): search `PATH`, then pack's directories (its bin directory, `$PACK_BIN_DIR` or else `~/.local/bin`, then the `bin` directory of pack's current collection under its state directory, if that exists), then on macOS and Linux `/opt/homebrew/bin` and `/usr/local/bin`, and on every platform `~/.idris2/bin`; with `#idris2.toolchain.preferPack#`, pack's directories come before `PATH`. Only absolute directories are searched (on Windows, ones with a drive or a `\\server\share` root). For pack's directories `~` is the `HOME` of the environment pack's wrappers run with (see `#idris2.toolchain.env#`). When set, only this value is used: an absolute path (on Windows, one with a drive or a `\\server\share` root; one without an extension is tried with the extensions of `PATHEXT`), or a bare command name looked up on `PATH`; if it names nothing, the tool is reported missing and no other place is searched. A leading `~` stands for your home directory. A workspace value applies only in a trusted workspace.

idris2.toolchain.lspPath.markdownDescription: Path to the `idris2-lsp` executable. Empty (the default): searched in the same places as `idris2` (see `#idris2.toolchain.idris2Path#`). When set, only this value is used: an absolute path (on Windows, one with a drive or a `\\server\share` root; one without an extension is tried with the extensions of `PATHEXT`), or a bare command name looked up on `PATH`; if it names nothing, the tool is reported missing and no other place is searched. A leading `~` stands for your home directory. A workspace value applies only in a trusted workspace.

idris2.toolchain.packPath.markdownDescription: Path to the `pack` executable. Empty (the default): searched in the same places as `idris2` (see `#idris2.toolchain.idris2Path#`). The extension never starts pack by itself; it only puts pack commands into a terminal for you to run. (pack's own `idris2` and `idris2-lsp` wrapper scripts call pack whenever they run, including when the extension reads their versions.) When set, only this value is used: an absolute path (on Windows, one with a drive or a `\\server\share` root; one without an extension is tried with the extensions of `PATHEXT`), or a bare command name looked up on `PATH`; if it names nothing, the tool is reported missing and no other place is searched. A leading `~` stands for your home directory. A workspace value applies only in a trusted workspace.

idris2.toolchain.preferPack.markdownDescription: Search pack's directories before `PATH` (see `#idris2.toolchain.idris2Path#`), so that `idris2` and `idris2-lsp` come from the same pack collection even when another `idris2` is first on `PATH`.

idris2.toolchain.env.markdownDescription: Environment variables for the `idris2`, `idris2-lsp` and `pack` processes the extension starts, for example `{ "IDRIS2_PREFIX": "/opt/idris2" }`. Each entry replaces the inherited variable of the same name; values are used as written, without `~` or variable expansion. The search for the executables reads `PATH` (and `PATHEXT` on Windows) and pack's `HOME`, `XDG_*` and `PACK_*` directory variables from this environment too. A workspace value applies only in a trusted workspace.

semanticTokenTypes.description: An escape hatch such as believe_me or assert_total (Idris 2 decoration `postulate`).

walkthroughs.title: Get Started with Idris 2
walkthroughs.description: Find the Idris 2 toolchain, install what is missing, and open a project.

steps.title: Find the Idris 2 toolchain
steps.description:
The extension looks for `idris2`, `idris2-lsp` and `pack` on this machine. Setup Information shows what it found and where.
[Show Setup Information](command:idris2.showSetupInformation)

steps.title: Install what is missing
steps.description:
The extension installs nothing by itself: each command opens a terminal with the install command typed in for you to review and run, or opens the installation instructions.
[Install Idris 2…](command:idris2.installIdris2)
[Install pack…](command:idris2.installPack)
[Install or Update idris2-lsp with pack](command:idris2.installIdris2Lsp)

steps.title: Open an Idris 2 project
steps.description:
Open the folder of your package (the directory with its `.ipkg` file), or any folder of `.idr` files.
[Open Folder](command:workbench.action.files.openFolder)

scripts.vscode:prepublish: npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.mjs --production
scripts.compile: npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.mjs
scripts.pretest: npm run compile-tests && npm run compile
scripts.test:e2e: npm run compile-tests && npm run compile && vscode-test --label e2e
scripts.test:corpus: node scripts/fetch-corpus.mjs && npm run compile-tests && mocha --ui tdd out/test/grammar/corpus.test.js
